question: Print a three-line introduction card for JavaScript. Put the name, the year it was created and its main job into variables, then log one line each.
Create an object called js holding name, year and type, then print each property on its own line. Example: { name: "JavaScript", year: 1995, type: "interpreted" }
Build one version string from three variables (name, edition, year) and log the single line. Example: name="JavaScript", edition="ECMAScript", year=2023 gives a single sentence.
Make an array of four places JavaScript runs: "browser", "Node.js", "Deno", "Bun". Print each one on its own line using a loop, not four separate logs.
Print what each layer of a web page is responsible for. Define HTML, CSS and JavaScript as short description strings and log each one.
Write a function introduce() that logs the name, the purpose and the two places the language runs. Give it no parameters and call it once.
Print the string "JavaScript" and how many characters it has. Use the .length property rather than counting by hand.
Create a metadata object for a script file with filename, language and runCommand. Print all three, for example filename "app.js" runCommand "node app.js".
Write a program that sets two flags, isInterpreted = true and isJIT = true, builds one summary string from them and logs that single string.
List three reasons a beginner should learn JavaScript (fast feedback, big job market, runs everywhere) and print them as a numbered list built in a loop.
Write a function describe(value) that returns the text "number" or "text" based on typeof, then log the result for 42 and for "42".
Print a type report for a list of values: 1, "a", true, null, undefined, [1], {}. Use typeof on each and log value, space, type.
answer:
typeof works on every value, including null and arrays. Loop over the list and print the type beside each value.

code:
const values = [1, "a", true, null, undefined, [1], {}];
for (const value of values) {
  console.log(String(value), "->", typeof value);
}

output:
1 -> number
a -> string
true -> boolean
null -> object
undefined -> undefined
1 -> object
[object Object] -> object

Predict the output: log [1,2,3] + [4,5,6], log {a:1} + {a:1}, and log the result of spreading an array into a new one.
Predict the output: log a string with a trailing comma, log the string "5" repeated 3 times, and log an object built with both dot and bracket notation.
